subject: BeyondCare private cluster: throttling, elevated p95 & 5xx surge — mitigation plan
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@beyondcare.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@beyondcare.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production spike — private cluster showing throttling and 5xx

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency (now ~1.8s from ~420ms) and a rise in 5xx responses across multiple routes on our private deployment in us-west-2 starting at ~08:45 PT. Throughput looks capped (requests/sec dropped ~40%) despite no change in traffic from our side. Attached are a short dump of request ids and the kafka ingest metrics we pulled.

Full impact: product search and patient-record retrieval routes are intermittently timing out. We have customers on support calls. Can Redwood run an emergency triage and tell us expected ETA for a fix? If needed we can accept a short maintenance window.

Attachments: request_ids_20261120.log (text), kafka_ingest_metrics_20261120.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Mehta
Director of Engineering, BeyondCare
rajiv@beyondcare.ai
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@beyondcare.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — private cluster showing throttling and 5xx

Thanks for the heads-up, Rajiv — apologies for the disruption.

Quick acknowledgements and immediate asks:
- I’ve flagged this for Rishi (infra lead) and Grace (CS) to coordinate with you live.
- Can you confirm whether you pushed any model updates or config changes in the last 24h?
- Please share: current desired concurrency, model id/version you’re pinned to, and the exact routes that are failing (we have the request ids, thank you).

Initial plan (we can start immediately once we have permission):
1) Short maintenance window (5–15m) to temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens and increase worker count to relieve queueing.
2) If that doesn’t restore throughput, we propose a fast fallback to a verified quantized model variant (compat checked) to drop per-token execution time.
3) Rishi will pull kernel and queue metrics and propose a targeted kernel recompile if needed — that’s a ~45–90m operation with a short disruption.

If you approve step (1) now we’ll begin the change and keep the window as short as possible. We can also stand up a redirected hosted endpoint as immediate fallback if you prefer.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@beyondcare.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — private cluster showing throttling and 5xx

Timelines and technical triage notes (initial):
- Observed: GPU utilization on worker nodes is flat/under 70%, but there is a sustained kernel queue backlog and elevated host-side CPU sys time. KV cache hit rate dropped from ~92% to ~45% around 08:42. Kafka ingress shows a small burst of malformed trace-enriched payloads (attached by customer).
- Hypothesis: sudden cold-KV churn + heavier per-request preprocessing from the customer’s new trace fields is increasing host-side CPU and serialization latency, which is causing worker queues to back up and trigger request timeouts.

Immediate mitigations we can apply in <10m (with permission):
1) Reduce max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 and set max_concurrency per-worker +2 to trade batch efficiency for latency.
2) Temporarily enable aggressive KV caching TTL bump (client-side key persistence) if their workload will allow it.
3) Fallback: hot-swap to the quantized v0.9-qs model (compatible with their prompt schema) if point 1/2 fail.

If still failing, next step is to schedule a kernel recompile with tighter kernel selection and lowered kernel-preemption threshold — that requires a maintenance window (45–90m) and will be performed by infra ops.

I’ll start gathering kernel traces now. Marcus: can you prepare a rollback plan and quick hosted fallthrough endpoint? Grace: please prepare customer comms and credits options.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@beyondcare.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — private cluster showing throttling and 5xx

Rajiv — thanks. We’re authorized to proceed with the short mitigation (1) now and will hold off on the kernel recompile until we validate. Plan we’ll execute in the next 10 minutes:
- Apply reduced max_batch_tokens and increase worker concurrency.
- Monitor p95 and 5xx in real-time; we’ll post live updates into this thread.
- Prepare fallback hosted endpoint (Marcus) if we need to pivot.

Please confirm you’re OK with the 5–15m maintenance window and we’ll start immediately. If you prefer we can switch to hosted fallback instead of an in-cluster change — let us know.

—Kim
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@beyondcare.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Voronov <anya@beyondcare.ai>, support@beyondcare.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T09:52:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — private cluster showing throttling and 5xx

Kimberly — do the maintenance now. We need this fixed immediately. Our execs are on the line; copying Anya. We authorize the 5–15m window and also want you to stage the hosted fallback concurrently so we can failover if needed. We expect a full post-mortem and SLA credit assessment.

Also: please escalate to your engineering leadership — we need a named contact for exec-to-exec updates while the change is underway.

Rajiv
Rajiv Mehta
Director of Engineering, BeyondCare
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@beyondcare.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-action summary, timeline and next steps — BeyondCare private cluster incident

Hi Rajiv / Anya — following up with a concise timeline, actions taken, and next steps. Posting here so execs have a single place to review:

Timeline (short):
- 2026-11-20 08:42 PT — p95 and 5xx increase observed by BeyondCare.
- 2026-11-20 09:00 PT — Redwood infra triage began.
- 2026-11-20 09:10 PT — applied reduced max_batch_tokens and increased per-worker concurrency. Immediate p95 improvement to ~650ms; 5xx reduced by ~80%.
- 2026-11-20 09:40 PT — staged hosted fallback; not required.
- 2026-11-20 10:15 PT — KV cache TTL change applied; sustained improvement.

Actions completed:
- Short mitigations (batch/concurrency) applied and validated.
- Infra collected kernel traces and CPU profiles; preliminary signal points to host-side preprocessing overhead and KV churn.
- Preventative: scheduled kernel tuning and a controlled kernel recompile on 2026-11-22 02:00 PT (45m maintenance window).

Customer remediation items (we propose):
- One-time SLA credit (we’ll draft numbers; Kimberly will own the credit offer).
- Joint post-mortem with BeyondCare engineering and Redwood infra (invite to be scheduled).
- Recommended workload changes: trim trace enrichment fields at ingress or offload heavy preprocessing to async pipelines.

Links and artifacts: INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8421, runbook: redwood_runbook_private_maintenance.pdf, metrics: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/support/beyondcare/metrics-20261120

Action owners:
- Kimberly: customer credit / exec communications.
- Rishi: kernel tuning & ops plan.
- Marcus: hosted fallback test & rollback playbook.
- Grace: schedule and run the post-mortem meeting.

We’ll follow up with the post-mortem report after the kernel tuning run. Please flag if you need an exec briefing call; we can make time.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
